<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 1 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Wonderful Wizard of Oz ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Oz
* Place type: Country
* Isolation: Cut off from the rest of the world, never civilized

The Land of Oz is a country cut off from the rest of the world, a condition said to explain why witches and wizards still dwell there when, in the civilized countries, none are said to remain. Within its bounds live at least four witches: those of the North and South, described as good, and those of the East and West, described as wicked. After the Witch of the East is killed, only the Wicked Witch of the West remains as the land's sole remaining wicked witch. Regions of the Land of Oz are marked by distinct local dress; travelers nearing the Emerald City encounter people clothed in emerald-green and wearing peaked hats like those of the Munchkins. Dorothy is brought to the Land of Oz by a cyclone that carries her away from the gray country of Kansas, and she later recounts to the Witch how the cyclone brought her there and how she found her companions. Toto, who accompanies her, is said not to care whether he is in Kansas or the Land of Oz so long as Dorothy is with him.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 2 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Marvelous Land of Oz ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Oz
* Place type: Country
* Regions: Country of the Gillikins, land of the Munchkins
* Ruler: Scarecrow (His Majesty)

The Land of Oz is a country bordered by a wide, sandy desert that separates it from the rest of the world. Within its borders lie distinct regions, including the Country of the Gillikins in the north and the land of the Munchkins, recognizable by its blue houses and fences. Nearly all farm houses across the Land of Oz share a round, dome-shaped construction. At the time of these events, the Scarecrow holds the throne as His Majesty and is regarded as the wisest personage in the Land of Oz. His rule is challenged when General Jinjur assembles an army — a regiment of girls gathered from the four corners of the Land of Oz — to conquer him and seize the throne. Glinda the Good, described as a mighty Sorceress, is said to have such command of magic that nothing occurring anywhere in the Land of Oz escapes her notice.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 3 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Ozma of Oz / A Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Ev
* Place type: kingdom
* Region: across the desert from the Land of Oz, bordered to the north by a great mountain

The Land of Ev is a kingdom whose royal family was held in long imprisonment, their liberation being the stated purpose of Ozma's expedition there. The country lies beyond a dangerous desert from the Land of Oz, a stretch crossed by means of a magic carpet. Its landscape includes a valley lying between two high mountains, with a third great mountain blocking the valley and forming the northern edge of Ev; the Nome King's palace was said to lie underneath that mountain. After the royal family's release, the new King of Ev pledged his gratitude to Ozma and promised to render the Land of Oz any service within his power.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 4 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Oz
* Ruler: Princess Ozma

The Land of Oz is a marvelous country, reached by travelers such as the Wizard and Dorothy after passing through many queer countries in their travels. Access to Oz is tied to the Magic Belt, by which Princess Ozma can bring travelers to herself in the Land of Oz once a sign is given. Within Oz stands a palace containing an enchanted picture, through which Ozma observes distant events at a set hour, and a room where Dorothy stays as a guest. The land also hosts courtly ceremony: at a grand procession, Princess Ozma placed her own coronet upon the winner of a race, proclaiming the Sawhorse "Prince of Horses" and declaring that hereafter all other horses in the Land of Oz must be considered imitations by comparison, before riding at the head of the procession back to the city.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 5 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Road to Oz ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Oz
* Place type: Country
* Status: Unreachable by ordinary means

The Land of Oz is a country lying beyond the Deadly Sands, a barrier desert that "will Turn Any Living Flesh to Dust in an Instant." A sign at the edge of the sands names it "the LAND OF OZ" and states that "no one can Reach that Beautiful Country because of these Destroying Sands." Dorothy confirms the danger of the sands from her own experience, saying "it's true no one can live who tries to walk upon the sands." The Land of Oz encompasses the Emerald City, which Dorothy identifies as a place where she has friends who "would take care of them and send them safe home again."
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Emerald City of Oz ==

=== Infobox ===

* Name: Land of Oz
* Notable landmark: the Water of Oblivion

The Land of Oz is described as always beautiful, wherever one might go, even in its stranger, unfamiliar reaches where no houses or farmers can be found to guide travelers. It is home to unusual peoples, among them Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles, said to be the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz. Unlike the wider world, where people sail upon oceans for weeks without sighting land, there is no such thing as an ocean anywhere in the Land of Oz.
</div>

== Appearance ==

Among the notable features of the Land of Oz is a spring whose water seems clear and sparkling, bubbling up in a golden basin. Despite this inviting appearance, Ozma gravely declares it the most dangerous thing in all the Land of Oz, naming it the Water of Oblivion. Beyond such landmarks, travelers moving through unfamiliar parts of the country find no paths, houses, or farmers to guide them, even while the land itself remains beautiful throughout.

== Events ==

During their travels, Dorothy and the Wizard discuss airships, and the Wizard reveals he is working on a magic recipe meant to keep airships from ever reaching the Land of Oz. Elsewhere, the First and Foremost of the Phanfasms calls to conquer the Land of Oz, marshaling his Phanfasms in battle array and marching them into a tunnel toward the Emerald City. The Nome King's forces are ultimately turned back: General Guph is ordered to follow his master, the Nome King, and the Nomes quit the Land of Oz forever. The Phanfasms, Whimsies, and Growleywogs remain behind for a time, filling the gardens in such numbers that they trample the flowers and grass underfoot.

== Trivia ==

* No ocean exists anywhere in the Land of Oz, unlike the wider world beyond it.
* The Fuddlecumjig and the Fuddles are said to be the most peculiar people in all the Land of Oz.
* The spring known as the Water of Oblivion is described as the most dangerous thing in the entire Land of Oz.
